title: What is known about 1RB---_1LC0LD_1RD0LB_0RF1RE_1RF0RA_0LE0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1LC0LD_1RD0LB_0RF1RE_1RF0RA_0LE0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine converts long runs of short words one into another, a word at a time at the right end and a run at a time when walking back; the runs it leaves behind have nearly doubling lengths, but the exact map has not been found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 52,266 cells have been visited and 29,986 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498).

claims.title: Steady conversion and doubling runs
claims.text: Between 1.6·1010 and 2·1010 steps the tape ends in (1011)^X (10)^Y with X falling by 800 and Y rising by 2,400 every 4,000 right-end visits; the runs before it have lengths 221, 585, 650, 3,828, 2,242, 1,117, 555, 4,498, 3,791, 4,143, 3,966, 1,982, 991.

claims.title: No halt in the first 9.91×10<sup>830</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 9.91×10830 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.02×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 11,285 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_0RC1RD_0LD0RA_1RC0RE_1RF---_1LA0LB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

facts.text: lengths of consecutive frozen runs: nearly doubling.
No halt in the C simulator; 52,266 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.02×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Runs converted one by one
html: The tape is a sequence of long runs of the words 1011, 0111, 10 and 01. Most of the time the head works at the right end, where the tape ends in (1011)^X (10)^Y: every fifth visit, one 1011 becomes three 10. When a run is used up, the head walks left converting whole runs from one word to another.

The runs left behind have lengths close to a doubling sequence (about 990, 1,980, 3,970, 7,940), and the last run is much longer still. That looks like a binary counter, or a map that doubles a value at each level, but the exact phases and their halting condition have not been worked out.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498).
After 109 steps the tape spans 52,266 cells (14 left of the start, 37,397 right), with a density of 1s of 0.574.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Long runs of 4-cell and 2-cell words, converted run by run; at the end one 1011 becomes three 10 every five visits, and the runs left behind have nearly doubling lengths (991, 1981, 3966, 7939): a binary-like hierarchy, not decoded.
